prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. One finished landscape 3:2 full-bleed picture-book illustration, one explanatory comparison diagram. Allow only the distinct views, stages or comparison panels explicitly authored in this page's illustration brief, with their exact relationships and counts. No unrequested panels, insets, annotations or contact sheet. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
 No named child cast: Kit and Zoe MUST NOT appear. Include unnamed human workers/adults ONLY when explicitly required by this particular scene; otherwise show only the natural subjects. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: People Power; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: Three factual adult demonstrations: a level traffic-free park cycle path, a quiet enclosed ice rink, and a calm lake. Cyclist: medium-brown skin, short straight black hair under a plain yellow helmet, teal jacket, navy pants, white shoes; red upright chain-driven bicycle. Skater: light-brown skin, short curly dark hair, blue helmet, orange jacket, dark-green pants, black ice skates with one metal blade each. Rower: deep-brown skin, close-cropped black hair, purple shirt, navy pants and orange life jacket; green broad stable rowboat with two tan oars pivoted in the gunwales. No motors, races, steep slopes, roads, cultural costumes, flags or logos.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Red pedal bicycle with two wheels, visible chain and rear sprocket; Black ice skates with single silver blades, not wheels; Green rowboat with bow pointing right, rower facing left, two tan pivoted oars; Cyclist/skater helmets and rower life jacket retained in every view
 Input references lock identity, prop design and location; compose a NEW image for the exact scene, never reproduce the reference-board layout. The reference and overall prop list may contain finished objects and later story events: these are DESIGN REFERENCES ONLY, not permission to show them now. Show only the people, objects and specific stages explicitly required below; the declared diagram permits no other scenes or story events.
Page 8. Printed prose (NOT text to put in art): Legs push. Arms pull.
People power all three rides.
Required illustration: Closing three-part comparison diagram in the same left-to-right order as opening, with new poses: cyclist pressing pedal, skater starting a sideways push and rower starting a pull. Keep path, ice and lake separate. The effort in legs or arms is visible; no motors, labels or arrows.
Exact current state: Return to three rides with their common human power made visible.
Do not add events or stages beyond the authored diagram. Repeat a subject only when the authored comparison or cutaway requires it. No written title; the app renders live text.

visualReview.note: Closing authored comparison returns to all three human efforts. Correct surfaces, appropriate gear and stable identities make the common people-power synthesis clear. Producer independently inspected the final installed WebP natively; complete final sequence and relevant native diagrams were independently reviewed.
